chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to me wanting food or a sale on credit (nasi'ah), and I do not have it. Is it permissible for me to sell it to him on credit and fix its price, then buy it from another place and deliver it to him? He said, 'There is no harm with it.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods on credit when you do not currently possess them?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the permissibility of 'bai al-nasi'ah' (credit sale) where the seller fixes the price and delivers goods later, even if they do not yet possess the specific items, validating the mechanism of selling what one intends to acquire. It reflects the practical commercial flexibility recognized by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in early Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing this from the prohibition of selling what one does not own (bai al-ma'dum) when the intent is immediate transfer of ownership rather than mere speculation. The ruling underscores the validity of conditional sales in trade, provided the price is fixed and the transaction is free from major defects.
